notes: Sourced from Optoma's official spec sheet PDF (rear-panel connector diagram, items 1-20, and "I/O Connection Ports" / "Control" spec tables). HDMI 2.0 input supports HDCP 2.2 and 4K UHD (3840x2160); HDMI 1.4a input is limited to WUXGA (1920x1200) per the "Maximum Input Resolution" spec — grade set to hdmi-1.4 accordingly. The "HDMI out" port has no version specified in the spec sheet (likely a pass-through/loop-out at HDMI 1.4a level) so grade is omitted for it. USB service port is a mini/type-B service port per manual (used for firmware only) - no data-transfer USB version stated, so no grade assigned. The two USB-A ports are 5V/1.5A power-only outputs (no host/data functionality mentioned) - graded as bidirectional per instruction but no data-rate grade stated so omitted. VGA in doubles as YPbPr component input (shared 15-pin D-sub). AC power inlet type not explicitly named as "IEC" in the spec sheet, but rear-panel icon and included detachable "AC power cord" (100-240V auto-switching) are consistent with a standard IEC C14 inlet, common for this power class (530W); inferred with high confidence but not explicitly labeled "IEC" in the source. 3D Sync In/Out are typically mini-DIN (3-pin) connectors in Optoma's lineup, not in the provided connector list - mapped to closest available id (trs-3.5) is not a good fit either, so noted here as a caveat rather than force-mapped incorrectly; see below.

ports.name: HDBaseT In

ports.note: Network/control port; speed not stated in spec sheet

ports.note: 12V DC trigger output; closest available id, likely a small screw-terminal or 3.5mm DC jack in practice

ports.name: 3D Sync In
ports.note: Typically a mini-DIN 3-pin VESA 3D sync connector on Optoma projectors; no exact id in allowed list, mapped to closest (ir) as a control-signal port

ports.name: 3D Sync Out (5V)
ports.note: Same caveat as 3D Sync In - closest available id used, not a literal IR port

ports.name: AC Power
ports.note: 100-240V auto-switching AC input; detachable IEC power cord included in box
